verdict.rationale: Mistral's own docs cover reasoning models that generate chains of thought and spend extra compute time on harder problems. That is a first-party extended-thinking capability. However, the evidence never shows a documented request parameter for switching thinking on or off or setting effort, so the controllability part of the story is unproven. Missing for 10: documented request parameters for reasoning mode or effort level, confidence or logprob signals, a thinking budget control, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can control how hard the model thinks — extended reasoning/thinking modes, effort levels, or confidence signals — through documented request parameters

citations.quote: Reasoning strengthens this characteristic by going through training steps that encourage the model to generate chains of thought freely before producing the final answer
This allows models to explore the problem more profoundly and ultimately reach a better solution to the best of their ability by using extra compute time to generate more tokens
